2.text: uprightness--is the fruit of fearing God, as falsehood and ill-nature (Pro 2:15; Pro 3:32) of despising Him and His law.

3.text: rod of pride--that is, the punishment of pride, which they evince by their words. The words of the wise procure good to them.

4.text: crib is clean--empty; so "cleanness of teeth" denotes want of food (compare Amo 4:6). Men get the proper fruit of their doings (Gal 6:7).

5.text: A faithful witness, &c.--one tested to be such. utter lies--or, "breathe out lies"--that is, habitually lies (Pro 6:19; compare Act 9:1). Or the sense is, that habitual truthfulness, or lying, will be evinced in witness-bearing.

6.text: An humble, teachable spirit succeeds in seeking (Pro 8:9; Joh 7:17; Jam 1:5-6).

7.text: Avoid the society of those who cannot teach you.

8.text: Appearances deceive the thoughtless, but the prudent discriminate.

9.text: Fools make a mock at sin--or, "Sin deludes fools." righteous . . . favour--that is, of God, instead of the punishment of sin.

10.text: Each one best knows his own sorrows or joys.

11.text: (Compare Pro 12:7). The contrast of the whole is enhanced by that of house and tabernacle, a permanent and a temporary dwelling.

12.text: end thereof--or, "reward," what results (compare Pro 5:4). ways of death--leading to it.

13.text: The preceding sentiment illustrated by the disappointments of a wicked or untimely joy.

14.text: filled . . . ways--receive retribution (Pro 1:31). a good man . . . himself--literally, "is away from such," will not associate with him.

15.text: The simple . . . word--He is credulous, not from love, but heedlessness (Pro 13:16).

16.text: (Compare Pro 3:7; Pro 28:14). rageth--acts proudly and conceitedly.

17.text: He . . . angry--literally, "short of anger" (compare Pro 14:29, opposite idea). man . . . hated--that is, the deliberate evildoer is more hated than the rash.

18.text: inherit--as a portion (compare Pro 3:35). are crowned--literally, "are surrounded with it," abound in it.

19.text: Describes the humbling of the wicked by the punishment their sins incur.

20.text: This sad but true picture of human nature is not given approvingly, but only as a fact.

21.text: For such contempt of the poor is contrasted as sinful with the virtuous compassion of the good.

22.text: As usual, the interrogative negative strengthens the affirmative. mercy and truth--that is, God's (Psa 57:3; Psa 61:7).

23.text: labour--painful diligence. talk . . . penury--idle and vain promises and plans.

24.text: (Compare Pro 3:16). foolishness . . . folly--Folly remains, or produces folly; it has no benefit.

25.text: Life often depends on truth-telling. a deceitful . . . lies--He that breathes out lies is deceit, not to be trusted (Pro 14:5).

26.text: The blessings of piety descend to children (Pro 13:22; Pro 20:7; Exo 20:6).

27.text: (Compare Pro 13:14). fear of the Lord--or, "law of the wise," is wisdom (Psa 111:10).

28.text: The teaching of a true political economy.

29.text: slow . . . understanding--(Compare Pro 14:17). hasty--(Compare Pro 14:17). exalteth folly--makes it conspicuous, as if delighting to honor it.

30.text: A sound heart--both literally and figuratively, a source of health; in the latter sense, opposed to the known effect of evil passions on health.

31.text: reproacheth his Maker--who is the God of such, as well as of the rich (Pro 22:2; Job 31:15; and specially Sa1 2:8; Psa 113:7).

32.text: driven--thrust out violently (compare Psa 35:5-6). hath hope--trusteth (Pro 10:2; Pro 11:4; Psa 2:12), implying assurance of help.

33.text: resteth--preserved in quietness for use, while fools blazon their folly (Pro 12:23; Pro 13:16).

34.text: Righteousness--just principles and actions. exalteth--raises to honor. is a reproach--brings on them the ill-will of others (compare Pro 13:6).

35.text: wise--discreet or prudent. causeth shame-- (Pro 10:5; Pro 12:4) acts basely. Next: Proverbs Chapter 15

paragraphs: Every wise, &c.--literally, "The wisdoms" (compare Pro 9:1) "of women," plural, a distributive form of speech.
buildeth . . . house--increases wealth, which the foolish, by mismanagement, lessen.
